author: San_David
body:
Tl;dr Version: Create a thread for asking quick questions and providing quick answers, so people don't make threads asking one single question like this one. Will make forums less "spammy." Should be created after posting on this thread that you're going to make it, don't want five people creating something like this all at once. Should be created by a staff member, preferably.

-----------------

Long Version: Basically, a thread should be made that serves as a place where you can ask a small question and get an answer from another member of the community. You can ask questions like...

- Can you do "so-and-so" with the YML?
- Why isn't the server up right now?
- What's a good thread to learn how to rush in Nebula?

...and other simple questions like that. Questions that can be given a straight, factual answer, or a link to another thread explaining the answer to something. However, it might not be a good idea to include questions that include opinion, or may be biased in one way or another, like...

- What should I change my skin to?
- What's a good idea for a map?
- Can I join someone's clan / map making team?
- Why do I hate cake? .-.

Stuff like that deserves it's own thread, or, in the case of the cake question, should be answered by some psychologist, because there's something wrong there...

Anyways, a thread like this should probably be stickied and should never be locked unless the person who created the thread wants to pass it on to someone else or something like that.

One last thing is that, if someone wants to create a thread like this, they should probably post on this thread, so that there aren't five people creating it all at once. It should also be created by staff member, or someone with a good understanding of what the rules for this thread would be.

replies.author: San_David
replies.body:
Just thought I'd mention this as a secondary post, and not as an edit...

The reason for all of the precautions here, like having a moderator make it, is that a thread like this can probably get spammy fairly quickly. It would be best if the person who created the thread had some idea of what they were doing with it.

Not to mention, it would be preferable if this was that type of thread that wouldn't get locked, ever, unless the person who created it wanted to pass it on to someone else.
